summary.intent: Run the full autonomous post-execute-phase ship loop (verify, secure, validate, simplify, SDK E2E gate, CodeRabbit, ship, resolve PR reviews) for GSD phase 77 in the cipher-box repo, triaging every finding via a strict fix/todo/discard rule without user babysitting.
summary.outcome: Verification was already passing; the secure gate completed successfully — built a threat register from all 10 phase PLANs (all mitigate/accept dispositions, ASVS L1), qualified for the L1 short-circuit, spot-checked the highest-severity mitigations (zeroization, TEE rename, assertRootOwnership) manually, wrote and committed 77-SECURITY.md. Parallel crypto/privacy review, general security sweep, and simplify scan agents were launched in the background, and the SDK E2E client build chain was kicked off; validate (step 3) onward is still pending.

repo: secure-phase's short-circuit rule: if threats_open==0 AND register_authored_at_plan_time==true AND asvs_level==1, skip spawning the gsd-security-auditor agent entirely and go straight to writing SECURITY.md — only spot-check manually as an extra safety measure.

Threat registers are authored at plan time inside each PLAN.md's <threat_model> block (STRIDE fields: threat_id, category, component, severity, disposition, mitigation_plan); SUMMARY.md's '## Threat Flags' section supplements them.

cipher-box's secure-phase auto-gate hook is disabled in config, but the ship-phase orchestration still requires running the security audit unconditionally for crypto-heavy phases — don't rely on the hook state alone to decide whether to run it.
SECURITY.md is written from a template at .claude/gsd-core/templates/SECURITY.md when in State B (no existing SECURITY.md but PLANs/SUMMARYs present).
workflow: When a security sweep flags a possibly-unused import/exception class (e.g. ForbiddenException), grep for other usages before treating it as a real finding — it was a false positive still used elsewhere in the services.

Launching independent review agents (crypto/privacy, general security, simplify) in parallel background tasks while running the GSD write-artifact gates inline keeps the long ship-phase loop from serializing unnecessarily.

friction: The secure-phase workflow's auto-gate hook was disabled, requiring the orchestrator to reason explicitly about whether to still run the security audit rather than relying on the hook to trigger it.
